subject: TTFT & streaming cadence: targets and next steps
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.inference.com>
To: Jackson Lee <jackson@finlytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming cadence targets

Hi Jackson — thanks again for the demo time this morning. Quick written recap and the ask so we can lock the pilot scope.

Recap of what we heard on the call:
- Primary UX requirement: streaming responses for multi-turn assist flows (users expect incremental tokens).
- Desired p95 TTFT: <= 150 ms (ideal). Acceptable p95 floor: <= 250 ms.
- Typical prompt size: ~400–600 tokens. Median response length: ~350 tokens; 90th pct ~1,000 tokens.
- Expected steady-state peak: ~80 concurrent active generations in US region; short bursts up to ~420 concurrent (10–30s).
- Target throughput: ~2.5k req/min sustained during business hours.
- Preference: SSE for simplicity on the frontend, but open to WebSocket if we need lower tail latency or bi‑directional control.

Clarifying asks / what we need from you: 
1) Confirm the p95 TTFT target that we should be engineering to (confirm 150 ms desired vs 250 ms acceptable).
2) Confirm preferred streaming transport (SSE vs WebSocket) and whether you need client-initiated cancel or patching mid-stream.
3) Provide a short sample of production traffic (anonymized logs or a synthetic trace): typical prompt length distribution, session lengths, and burst patterns.
4) Any blackout/maintenance windows or region-specific constraints?

What we'll deliver for the pilot (high level):
- Bench run with your sample payloads and our recommended model variant(s).
- Suggested chunk cadence and framing: initial guidance below; we will refine after we run your traces.
- Runbook + fallback plan (attached by Ben) covering warm pool sizing, concurrency limits, and fallback model routing.

Initial technical guidance (tentative):
- Streaming framing: send an initial small chunk as soon as first tokens are available (first-chunk within 1–2 RTTs).
- Chunk cadence target: 200–400 ms between user-visible chunks for responses > 300 tokens (tunable).
- Chunk size: target ~120–220 tokens per chunk after the initial priming chunk.
- Backpressure: prefer server-side pacing with client reassembly; we recommend SSE for easier CDN/proxy compatibility unless you need bidirectional control.

Next steps / timeline:
- Please reply with confirmation on the four clarifying asks above by Tue 2026-11-24 so we can schedule a perf run the following week.
- Ben (SE) will attach the runbook and a proposed warm-pool config.

Thanks — looking forward to locking scope.

—

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming cadence targets

Mina — thanks for the concise summary. TL;DR: we can confirm most items, plus a few clarifications below.

Confirmed:
- p95 TTFT goal: we want to aim for <= 150 ms if achievable with your optimized stack. If the pilot shows regressions > 200 ms p95 we need an automatic fallback to a smaller/cheaper model to preserve UX.
- Throughput and concurrency numbers match our internal estimates.
- SSE is preferred for our initial client (React-based webapp) to keep the integration simple.

Clarifying details / asks from our side:
1) WebSocket vs SSE tradeoff: we prefer SSE now but would like a short note on where you see SSE causing tail issues vs WS (we may want WS for mobile clients later).
2) Bursty traffic: our production traces show microbursts every 10–12 minutes where concurrent gens spike 5–6x for ~20–45s. We need to understand how you’d autoscale/burst without exceeding cost targets.
3) Cold starts: what warm-pool size do you recommend for the pilot to avoid cold-kick TTFT spikes?
4) Security/compliance: Maya Wexler (copied) will take the lead on the SOC/SLA checklist after the pilot scope is locked.

Attached is a small sample trace (anonymized) showing token distribution and session lengths. We’ll upload a more complete sample to the Drive link you provided by EOD Monday.

—
Jackson Lee

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: TTFT & streaming cadence targets

Jackson / Mina — attaching our preliminary runbook (ttft_runbook_v1.pdf) that outlines warm-pool sizing, concurrency knobs, and chunking heuristics. Highlights below.

Runbook highlights (summary):
- Warm pool: for pilot we recommend maintaining ~18 warm instances (equivalent to ~6 A100-ish GPUs depending on model family) in US region to smooth short bursts; this maps to expected steady-state + 30% buffer for microbursts.
- Autoscale: keep autoscale thresholds conservative (scale-up on sustained queue > 200 ms for 3 samples; scale-down after 90s idle).
- Chunking: send a small priming chunk (16–32 tokens) immediately; thereafter pace chunks every 200–300 ms when output rate supports it. Chunk token size target: 100–180 tokens after priming.
- TTFT: with the above and quantized model variants (int8 / q4_x), we estimate p95 TTFT in the 110–160 ms range on our test harness for prompts ~500 tokens. We’ll provide exact histograms after we run your traces.
- Fallbacks: transparent downgrade to a smaller model variant on overload (automated routing policy) + circuit-breaker that returns an abbreviated response with option to re-request full generation.
- Network notes: SSE plays nicely with common CDNs and load balancers. WS gives you lower tail for very chatty sessions and allows client-initiated control messages (e.g., edit/cancel mid-gen). If you plan to do client-side edit/resume, WS is preferable.

Attachment: ttft_runbook_v1.pdf (attached)

I’ll queue a perf run for next Wed once we have your full trace. If you want earlier synthetic runs I can run them against a sanitized sample this afternoon.
